methodology.description: Public draft-helper PPR redraft board. Player value and market cost are intentionally kept separate. Rankings blend broad expert consensus, current projections, recent independent expert boards and material preseason/news context; ADP is treated as price rather than player quality. League scoring, roster construction, draft slot, drafted players, positional scarcity and next-pick pressure are applied by the client recommendation engine.
rankingInputs: FantasyPros 2026 PPR consensus, injury feed and current market data checked Sept. 4
ESPN current 2026 fantasy rankings, draft guidance and NFL news checked Sept. 4
RotoWire Sept. 4 PPR/Yahoo rankings, health reports and player news
CBS Sports Sept. 4 analyst boards, projections and ADP context
NFL.com official injury/transaction reporting checked through Sept. 4
Rotoworld/NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, Fantasy Life and other independent market sources checked through Sept. 4
methodology.marketInput: Current PPR ADP remains a separate market-price input, cross-checked across RotoWire, FantasyPros, Sleeper-market samples, CBS/Yahoo and other platform references through Sept. 4. ADP is treated as price, not as a substitute for player value; large gaps remain when injury, availability, role uncertainty or expert disagreement justifies them.
newsInputs: Saquon Barkley moves from No. 19 to No. 16. RotoWire's Sept. 4 board has him No. 13 and the freshest broad FantasyPros overall sample has him No. 16. The prior No. 19 value had become too conservative relative to the current independent center.

Puka Nacua remains No. 4, but confidence improves after returning to practice and avoiding the Commissioner's Exempt List for now. The soft-tissue history and potential later discipline review still justify a wider downside range than the other top-five players.

Ashton Jeanty remains No. 23. He missed Wednesday practice, but Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic Jeanty will play Week 1. RotoWire's Sept. 4 board has him No. 22, so the public helper keeps the value rank essentially at the fresh market-independent center rather than chasing his more aggressive ADP.

Jeremiyah Love remains No. 26 with slightly lower confidence. NFL Network described him as roughly 50/50 for Week 1, while RotoWire's Sept. 4 board has him No. 27. The rank remains stable but the short-term availability risk is now explicit.

Josh Jacobs remains deeply discounted while on the Commissioner's Exempt List. RotoWire's Sept. 4 board has him No. 99; Green Bay still expects him to play at some point in 2026, so the helper preserves a very wide range instead of assuming either a quick return or a lost season.
methodology.notes: Expert disagreement is preserved with expertHigh/expertLow ranges; unresolved injuries, discipline risk and genuine model disagreement can intentionally widen those ranges. Confidence reflects agreement plus news certainty, not ceiling. This file is used only by smhillis/sleeper-draft-helper-public and must not be copied into or used to modify Scott's personal Sleeper Draft Assistant.

players.name: Ja'Marr Chase
players.news: Present but did not participate in Wednesday practice after the recent left-knee hyperextension. Cincinnati still says it feels good about his progress, and fresh PPR boards continue to value him around No. 3 overall, so the rank holds while confidence and downside range widen.

players.name: Puka Nacua
players.news: Returned to practice after the psoas/groin soreness and is not on the Commissioner's Exempt List for now. Top-five season-long value remains intact, while the wider downside band stays because of soft-tissue history and unresolved potential discipline review.

players.name: Jonathan Taylor
players.news: CBS is aggressively bullish while RotoWire is more conservative, so the value rank holds and the disagreement band remains broad.

players.name: Christian McCaffrey
players.news: Still carries elite weekly projection upside, but fresh independent boards and workload concerns keep the cross-source center below his market price.

players.name: De'Von Achane
players.news: Projection-driven boards remain bullish while more conservative expert boards preserve a much lower floor. The higher value rank does not erase durability and offensive-environment disagreement.

players.name: Derrick Henry
players.news: Current expert boards still disagree mainly on age-driven downside, but the cross-source center remains in the mid-teens.

players.name: Kenneth Walker III
players.news: Current rankings remain supportive after the late-preseason foot concern was described as unlikely to alter his normal workload materially.

players.name: Saquon Barkley
players.news: Fresh Sept. 4 boards moved the cross-source center upward: RotoWire has him No. 13 and the freshest broad FantasyPros overall sample has him No. 16. The helper corrects the prior No. 19 value while still preserving age/workload downside.

players.name: Rashee Rice
players.news: Projection-driven boards remain bullish while other experts are far lower, leaving one of the widest disagreement ranges in the top 30.

players.name: Ashton Jeanty
players.news: Did not practice Wednesday, but Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he is optimistic Jeanty will play Week 1. RotoWire's Sept. 4 board has him No. 22, so the helper holds No. 23 and keeps a broad downside range until he returns to full practice.

players.name: Jeremiyah Love
players.news: NFL Network described him as roughly 50/50 for Week 1 while he works back from the high-ankle sprain. RotoWire's Sept. 4 board has him No. 27, so the helper holds No. 26 but lowers confidence to reflect the near-term availability risk.

players.name: Nico Collins
players.news: Fresh expert work remains unusually divided, so the wide disagreement is explicitly preserved.

players.name: MarShawn Lloyd
players.news: Still the favorite to lead Green Bay's backfield while Josh Jacobs is unavailable, but the first post-news spike has cooled. ESPN's final PPR mock selected Lloyd 70th while RotoWire's Sept. 3 season-long PPR board has him 98th, so the helper moves him to No. 74 and preserves the wide disagreement rather than treating a temporary depth-chart promotion as guaranteed full-season value.

players.name: Josh Jacobs
players.news: Still on the Commissioner's Exempt List and unable to practice or play while listed. RotoWire's Sept. 4 board has him No. 99, while Green Bay's GM still expects him to play in 2026. The helper keeps No. 90 but widens the downside because the return timeline is controlled by the league, not the team.
